## The assignment

In class we built a house price model for Philadelphia. Now your team does it for a city you haven't modeled: **Chicago**.

The Cook County Assessor's Office has to value every home in the county, including the vast majority that didn't sell this year. Assessments drive property tax bills. When they're wrong in a systematic way, some households pay more than their share. A 2017 *Chicago Tribune* investigation, "The Tax Divide," found exactly that in Cook County: lower-value homes were assessed at higher shares of their worth than expensive ones.

Build a model that predicts **single-family sale prices in Chicago, 2023–2025**, using only the tools from this course. The file contains **only features of the house itself**. Everything about location is yours to build.

### A real test

| File | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `chicago_train.csv` | About 80% of the houses, **with** sale prices |
| `chicago_test.csv` | The other 20%, **without** sale prices. You predict them; we score you. |

The test houses were held out by house, not by sale, so a house that sold twice is entirely on one side. Your CV RMSE is your estimate. Your test RMSE is the truth. **If they're far apart, something leaked.** 

**Due:** Friday, October 30. All teammates renders the file on their portfolio and every member submits that link on Canvas. One teammate uploads `team_XX_predictions.csv`.

**Individual accountability:** Q7 on October 30 asks each of you about *this* model: which features you used and why, your CV and test RMSE, and where the model fails worst. Make sure everyone can explain all of it.

### Rules

::: {.callout-important}
## 1. Clean training rows once, in Part 1. Never drop test rows.
You must predict every test house, so fill NAs in a feature rather than filtering.

## 2. Stay inside the time window
Open data from 2023–2025 only.

## 3. No leakage
Nothing built from sale prices. *Would the Assessor have this number for a house that didn't sell?*

## 4. The outcome stays in dollars
Transform predictors, not `sale_price`.

## 5. No prices from the test fold or the future
No features built from other houses' sale prices. 
:::

### Please include in your final rendered qmd for this assignment:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Model log** | Every model you tried, in order, with CV RMSE and Moran's I. Each row has a note saying why you tried it. |
| **Features** | Incorporate the feature engineering tricks - including the spatial ones covered these past few weeks. 
| **Diagnostics** | Residual maps for your baseline and final model, and what changed. |
| **Error analysis** | Where your final model fails worst, and whose homes it over-values (Part 4). |
| **Reasoning** | Choices justified by evidence from your own analysis.

```{r}
#| label: helpers
check_na <- function(formula, df) {
  vars <- all.vars(formula)
  bad <- vars[sapply(vars, function(v) any(is.na(df[[v]])))]
  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    stop("These variables have NAs: ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "),
         ". Fill them or choose another variable (Rule 1).")
  }
}


cv_rmse <- function(formula, data) {
  df <- if (inherits(data, "sf")) st_drop_geometry(data) else data
  check_na(formula, df)
  set.seed(5080)
  fit <- train(formula, data = df, method = "lm",
               trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10))
  fit$results$RMSE
}


cv_pred <- function(formula, data) {
  df <- if (inherits(data, "sf")) st_drop_geometry(data) else data
  check_na(formula, df)
  set.seed(5080)
  fit <- train(formula, data = df, method = "lm",
               trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10,
                                        savePredictions = "final"))
  fit$pred %>% arrange(rowIndex) %>% pull(pred)
}


socrata_get <- function(dataset, where, select = NULL, limit = 200000) {
  where <- str_squish(where)
  q <- paste0("$where=", URLencode(where, reserved = TRUE), "&$limit=", limit)
  if (!is.null(select)) q <- paste0(q, "&$select=", URLencode(str_squish(select), reserved = TRUE))
  url <- paste0("https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/", dataset, ".geojson?", q)
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
  resp <- tryCatch(download.file(url, tmp, quiet = TRUE), error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(resp, "error")) stop("Portal request failed. Open this URL in a browser to see why:\n", url)
  st_read(tmp, quiet = TRUE)
}

```

### base model
```{r}

  mutate(
    Cat_bedroom_num = case_when(
      num_bedrooms <= 2 ~ "1-2 bedrooms",
      num_bedrooms == 3 ~ "3 bedrooms",
      num_bedrooms >= 4 & num_bedrooms <= 5 ~ "4-5 bedrooms",
      num_bedrooms >= 6 ~ "6+ bedrooms",
```

```{r}

coords_train <- st_coordinates(train_set)
w_knn <- nb2listw(knn2nb(knearneigh(coords_train, k = 5)), style = "W")


train_set$resid_m1 <- residuals(m1)

mc <- moran.mc(train_set$resid_m1, w_knn, nsim = 499)
mc$statistic
mc$p.value

model_log <- model_log %>%
  add_row(model = "m1", added = "baseline",
          cv_rmse = cv_rmse(f1, train_set),
          morans_i = mc$statistic,
          moran_p = mc$p.value,
          notes = "baseline model using squared building age, building square foot, and number of bedrooms by category.")

model_log
```

## Part 2: spatial model

### distance to L
```{r}
#| label: Model 2

L_stations <- st_read("https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/3tzw-cg4m.geojson") |>
  st_transform(st_crs(all_sales))

ggplot(L_stations) + geom_sf() #just checking


all_sales <- all_sales %>%
  mutate(L_500ft = lengths(st_intersects(st_buffer(., 500), L_stations)))

nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(all_sales$geometry, L_stations)

all_sales <- all_sales %>%
  mutate(dist_Lstation = as.numeric(
    st_distance(geometry, L_stations[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)))


ggplot(all_sales, aes(x = dist_Lstation, y = sale_price)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5)
ggplot(all_sales, aes(x = dist_Lstation)) + geom_histogram(bins = 30) + theme_minimal()
ggplot(all_sales, aes(x = L_500ft)) + geom_histogram(bins = 30) + theme_minimal()


train_sales <- all_sales %>% filter(split == "train")

f3 <- sale_price ~ I(building_age^2) + building_age + Cat_bedroom_num + Cat_fireplaces_num + building_sf + log_lotsize_sqft + dist_Lstation

m3 <- lm(f3, data = train_sales)
summary(m3)

train_set$resid_m3 <- residuals(m3)

mc <- moran.mc(train_set$resid_m3, w_knn, nsim = 499)
mc$statistic
mc$p.value


model_log <- model_log %>%
  add_row(model = "m3", added = "Station distance",
          cv_rmse = cv_rmse(f3, train_sales),
          morans_i = mc$statistic,
          moran_p = mc$p.value,
          notes = "Proximity to L metro")

model_log
```

#Bus stops
```{r}
crs_projected <- 3435
bus_stops <- st_read(
  "https://data.cityofchicago.org/api/v3/views/qs84-j7wh/query.geojson?accessType=DOWNLOAD",
  quiet = TRUE
) %>%
  st_transform(crs_projected) %>%
  filter(!st_is_empty(geometry))

all_sales <- all_sales %>%
  st_transform(crs_projected)

bus_knn <- st_nn(
  all_sales,
  bus_stops,
  k = 5,
  returnDist = TRUE,
  progress = FALSE
)

all_sales$bus_knn5 <- sapply(
  bus_knn$dist,
  mean
)

train_sales <- all_sales %>% filter(split == "train")

f5 <- sale_price ~ I(building_age^2) + building_age + Cat_bedroom_num + Cat_fireplaces_num + building_sf + log_lotsize_sqft + dist_Lstation + dist_cafe_seat + bus_knn5

m5 <- lm(f5, data = train_sales)
summary(m5)

train_set$resid_m5 <- residuals(m5)

mc <- moran.mc(train_set$resid_m5, w_knn, nsim = 499)
mc$statistic
mc$p.value

model_log <- model_log %>%
  add_row(model = "m5", added = "Bus Stops",
          cv_rmse = cv_rmse(f5, train_sales),
          morans_i = mc$statistic,
          moran_p = mc$p.value,
          notes = "+ bus knn5")

model_log
```

###+ crime

```{r}
#| eval: false
base_url <- "https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/ijzp-q8t2.json"

where_clause <- paste(
  "date >= '2023-01-01T00:00:00'",
  "AND date < '2024-01-01T00:00:00'",
  "AND latitude IS NOT NULL",
  "AND longitude IS NOT NULL"
)

limit_n <- 50000
offset_n <- 0
crime_list <- list()

repeat {
  res <- GET(
    base_url,
    query = list(
      `$where` = where_clause,
      `$select` = "date,latitude,longitude",
      `$limit` = limit_n,
      `$offset` = offset_n,
      `$order` = "date"
    )
  )

  stop_for_status(res)

  chunk <- fromJSON(
    content(res, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"),
    flatten = TRUE
  )

  if (nrow(chunk) == 0) break

  crime_list[[length(crime_list) + 1]] <- chunk
  message("Downloaded rows: ", offset_n + nrow(chunk))

  if (nrow(chunk) < limit_n) break

  offset_n <- offset_n + limit_n
}

crime_2023 <- bind_rows(crime_list)

```

#Education and Elderly
```{r}

#| label: Demographic Variables

vars <- load_variables(2022, "acs5")

chicago_tracts <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = "IL",
  county = "Cook",
  variables = c(                 # universe #
    total_pop = "B01003_001",    # people
    totalHH = "B08201_001",      # households
    #medinc = "B07011_001",       # people
    under18 = "C18108_002",      # people
    adult_18_64 = "C18108_006",  # people
    over65 = "C18108_010",      # people
    edu_total  = "B15003_001",   # people >25yrs
    ba         = "B15003_022",   # people >25yrs
    ma         = "B15003_023",   # people >25yrs
    prof       = "B15003_024",   # people >25yrs
    phd        = "B15003_025"    # people >25yrs
  ),
    year = 2022,
  output = "wide",
  geometry = TRUE
) %>%
  st_transform(3435)
```
```{r}
#| label: Demographic Variables

#Transform
chicago_tracts <- chicago_tracts %>%
  mutate(
    pct_18to64 = adult_18_64E / total_popE * 100,
    pct_under18 = under18E / total_popE * 100,
    pct_over64 = over65E / total_popE * 100,
    pct_ba     = (baE + maE + profE + phdE) / edu_totalE * 100
    ) %>%
  mutate(pct_over64 = replace_na(pct_over64, 0),
         pct_ba     = replace_na(pct_ba, 0))


#Spatially Join Demographic Data
all_sales <- st_join(
  all_sales,
  chicago_tracts,
  join = st_within,
  left = TRUE
) 

#Replace NAs
over64_NA <- median(all_sales$pct_over64[all_sales$split == "train"], na.rm = TRUE)
                     
all_sales <- all_sales %>% mutate(pct_over64 = replace_na(pct_over64, over64_NA))

BA_NA <- median(all_sales$pct_ba[all_sales$split == "train"], na.rm = TRUE)
                     
all_sales <- all_sales %>% mutate(pct_ba = replace_na(pct_ba, BA_NA))


train_sales <- all_sales %>% filter(split == "train")

f8 <- sale_price ~ I(building_age^2) + building_age + Cat_bedroom_num + Cat_fireplaces_num + building_sf + log_lotsize_sqft + dist_Lstation + dist_cafe_seat  + crime_count_500feet + neighborhood_income + pct_over64 + pct_ba + I(pct_ba^2)

m8 <- lm(f8, data = train_sales)
summary(m8)

train_set$resid_m8 <- residuals(m8)
```

###refine our model

```{r}
#| label: common-data

library(sf)
library(spdep)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(caret)



numeric_predictors <- c(
  "building_age",
  "building_sf",
  "log_lotsize_sqft",
  "dist_Lstation",
  "dist_cafe_seat",
  "bus_knn5",
  "crime_count_500feet",
  "neighborhood_income",
  "pct_over64",
  "pct_ba",
  "dist_grocery",
  "dist_cbd"
)

factor_predictors <- c(
  "Cat_bedroom_num",
  "Cat_fireplaces_num",
  "community"
)


numeric_predictors <- intersect(
  numeric_predictors,
  names(all_sales)
)

factor_predictors <- intersect(
  factor_predictors,
  names(all_sales)
)



train_rows <- all_sales$split == "train"

impute_medians <- vapply(
  numeric_predictors,
  function(v) {
    x <- all_sales[[v]][train_rows]

    if (all(is.na(x))) {
      stop(paste(
        "All training values are missing for:", v,
        "- investigate this variable before fitting the models."
      ))
    }

    median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  },
  numeric(1)
)



model_data_common <- all_sales

for (v in numeric_predictors) {
  x <- model_data_common[[v]]

  x[is.na(x)] <- impute_medians[[v]]

  model_data_common[[v]] <- x
}



for (v in factor_predictors) {
  x <- as.character(model_data_common[[v]])

  x[is.na(x) | trimws(x) == ""] <- "Unknown"

  model_data_common[[v]] <- x
}



train_common <- model_data_common %>%
  filter(split == "train")

test_common <- model_data_common %>%
  filter(split == "test")


for (v in factor_predictors) {

  train_values <- as.character(train_common[[v]])
  test_values  <- as.character(test_common[[v]])


  known_levels <- unique(train_values[!is.na(train_values)])


  if (!"Unknown" %in% known_levels) {

    test_values[!test_values %in% known_levels] <- NA_character_

    if (anyNA(test_values)) {
      most_common <- names(
        sort(table(train_values), decreasing = TRUE)
      )[1]

      test_values[is.na(test_values)] <- most_common
    }

  } else {


    test_values[!test_values %in% known_levels] <- "Unknown"
  }


  train_common[[v]] <- factor(
    train_values,
    levels = known_levels
  )

  test_common[[v]] <- factor(
    test_values,
    levels = known_levels
  )
}



cat("Training rows:", nrow(train_common), "\n")
cat("Test rows:", nrow(test_common), "\n")


stopifnot(all(!is.na(train_common$sale_price)))
stopifnot(all(is.na(test_common$sale_price)))


predictor_vars <- c(numeric_predictors, factor_predictors)

na_check <- sapply(
  model_data_common %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    select(all_of(predictor_vars)),
  function(x) sum(is.na(x))
)

na_check
```

```{r}
#| label: refit-common-models

# Model formulas
model_formulas <- list(
  m1 = f1,
  m2 = f2,
  m3 = f3,
  m4 = f4,
  m5 = f5,
  m6 = f6,
  m7 = f7,
  m8 = f8,
  m9 = f9,
  m10 = f10,
  m11 = f11
)

train_common_df <- st_drop_geometry(train_common)


missing_by_model <- sapply(
  model_formulas,
  function(f) {
    vars <- all.vars(f)

    sum(
      !complete.cases(
        train_common_df[, vars, drop = FALSE]
      )
    )
  }
)

print(missing_by_model)

stopifnot(all(missing_by_model == 0))


models <- lapply(
  model_formulas,
  function(f) {
    lm(
      formula = f,
      data = train_common_df,
      na.action = na.fail
    )
  }
)

# Check sample sizes
sapply(models, nobs)
```

```{r}
#| label: common-cv-rmse

set.seed(5080)

cv_results <- lapply(
  names(model_formulas),
  function(model_name) {

    f <- model_formulas[[model_name]]

    tibble(
      model = model_name,
      cv_rmse = cv_rmse(f, train_common)
    )
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows()

cv_results
```

```{r}
#| label: morans-i


coords <- st_coordinates(train_common)


knn <- knearneigh(coords, k = 5)
neighbors <- knn2nb(knn)

w_knn <- nb2listw(
  neighbors,
  style = "W",
  zero.policy = TRUE
)


set.seed(5080)

moran_results <- lapply(
  names(models),
  function(model_name) {

    model <- models[[model_name]]
    residuals_model <- residuals(model)

    stopifnot(
      length(residuals_model) == nrow(train_common)
    )

    mc <- moran.mc(
      residuals_model,
      listw = w_knn,
      nsim = 499,
      zero.policy = TRUE
    )

    tibble(
      model = model_name,
      morans_I = as.numeric(mc$statistic),
      morans_p_value = mc$p.value
    )
  }
) %>%
  bind_rows()

moran_results
```

## Part 6: Reflection (about 300 words, as a team)

1. **Read one coefficient twice:** once as β̂, once for what it does to ŷ.
In our final model, Percent of people over 64 is 259.5194 (β). Therefore for every 1% increase in the share of elderly people in a census tract, there is a $259.52 increase in predicted sale price of a home, holding all other variables constant.


2. **Would you hand this model to the Assessor?** What would you warn them about?

This model does align with the Chicago Tribune's finding that lower-value homes were assessed at higher shares of their worth than expensive ones; while lower value homes had an under/over-value ratio of 0.459854, higher value homes had a ratio of 1.341135. Nevertheless, we still do not suggest that an Assessor to use this model.

First, our final model is still off by $273,157.80. This is an immense range and can skew future assessments to either over- or under-value a home in drastically incorrect ways.

Second, while our final model does seem to address issues of spatial autocorrelation from our baseline model, it over-fixes by now under-valuing a much larger share of homes.

Third, these are both indications that we are "missing something" -- either demographic, spatial, or some other metric -- that would help better explain sale price. On the other hand, we may have included features that though they contributed to the overall RMSE, they may not actually be useful variables going forward. For example, distance to groceries did not lower the RMSE so much and so may not be worth including in future models.

Finally, while a tax assessment model may help people lower their taxes, if it is an open source government model, it could be used by for-profit real estate companies to "game the market" in order to aquire under-taxed homes. There is no such thing as no-strings-attached in the real estate market.
